text.content:
Trigger: Severe stress or trauma striking a highly proficient thaumaturge whose mind has come to think natively in occult symbology.

Under sufficient tension, the afflicted thaumaturge reverts to speaking in tongues — not idiot babble, but genuine thaumaturgical symbology, words and phrases that translate abstract magical concepts the character may not even consciously understand. The character has no idea she's doing anything unusual; to her, the arcane words feel like ordinary speech, while she becomes wholly unable to produce or comprehend mundane language for the duration.

Other thaumaturges may recognize scattered fragments, but the full meaning eludes translation. Given time or concentration, the character reverts to normal speech with no memory of what she said. As with other derangements, a character may spend a Willpower point (System) or Trait (MET) to suppress an episode and speak normally for the rest of the scene, though the underlying condition remains until treated through extended therapy or dramatic roleplaying resolution. This is a difficult derangement to portray well; Storytellers are encouraged to reward players who evoke it as fractured, meaningful communication rather than mere gibberish.

Also listed for Storytellers under Rules Reference (Storyteller Only): @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.b50bed5f9d7b4ac2]{Thaumaturgical Glossolalia} (same write-up, kept there too for topical browsing).
